On September 21, the People’s Climate March was held in New York and around the world. In Korea, GEYK organized a march focused on energy issues, starting at Seoul City Hall and making its way to Jongno.

  1. South Korea had pledged to cut greenhouse gas emissions by 30% below business as usual by 2020. We called on the government to honor that commitment when it appeared ready to abandon it.
  2. We called for a higher share of renewable energy to prepare for international regulation. The United States, China, Japan, and many European countries were investing in renewables and reducing their reliance on oil, coal, and nuclear energy.
  3. We asked the Korean government to stop adding fossil-fuel power plants. We hoped this would send a clear message to a government moving in the opposite direction from other countries preparing for international regulation.

Through the march, GEYK informed the public about the realities of climate change and strengthened the resolve of citizens and government to tackle the climate crisis. We hoped the views of NGOs would reach local communities, national policymakers, and the international community.
